text: Breast health diet and exercise: Keep a healthy body weight through balanced meals and regular activity.
source: Source: American Cancer Society guidelines on diet and physical activity

text: Breast health diet and exercise: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate activity per week.
source: Source: American Cancer Society guidelines on diet and physical activity

text: Breast health diet and exercise: Eat plenty of vegetables, fruit, whole grains and legumes.
source: Source: American Cancer Society guidelines on diet and physical activity

text: Breast health diet and exercise: Limit processed and red meat, sugary drinks and highly processed foods.
source: Source: American Cancer Society guidelines on diet and physical activity

text: Breast health diet and exercise: Alcohol raises breast cancer risk, so it is best to avoid it or keep it very low.
source: Source: American Cancer Society guidelines on diet and physical activity

text: Breast health diet and exercise: Diet needs for people in cancer treatment are individual, so ask the oncology team or an oncology dietitian.
source: Source: American Cancer Society guidelines on diet and physical activity

text: Breast health diet and exercise: Any new breast lump, nipple change or skin change should be checked by a doctor promptly.
source: Source: American Cancer Society guidelines on diet and physical activity

text: Diabetes diet and exercise: Eat at regular times and avoid long gaps between meals, especially if taking glucose-lowering medicine.
source: Source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care; ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians

text: Diabetes diet and exercise: Prefer whole grains, millets, dal, beans, vegetables and fruit over refined flour, large portions of white rice and sweets.
source: Source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care; ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians

text: Diabetes diet and exercise: Limit added sugar, sweets, fruit juice and sugary drinks.
source: Source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care; ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians

text: Diabetes diet and exercise: Plate method: fill half the plate with non-starchy vegetables, a quarter with protein, and a quarter with whole grains.
source: Source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care; ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians

text: Diabetes diet and exercise: High-fibre foods such as dal, beans, oats and vegetables slow the rise in blood sugar.
source: Source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care; ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians

text: Diabetes diet and exercise: Limit alcohol and highly processed packaged foods.
source: Source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care; ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians

text: Diabetes diet and exercise: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity per week, such as brisk walking or cycling, spread over at least 3 days.
source: Source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care; ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians

text: Diabetes diet and exercise: Do not go more than 2 days in a row without activity.
source: Source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care; ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians

text: Diabetes diet and exercise: Add resistance exercise on 2 to 3 non-consecutive days per week.
source: Source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care; ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians

text: Diabetes diet and exercise: If you take insulin or certain tablets, check blood sugar around exercise and carry a fast-acting sugar source.
source: Source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care; ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians

text: Diabetes diet and exercise: Talk to a doctor or registered dietitian before changing medicines or starting a new exercise programme.
source: Source: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care; ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians

text: Heart health diet and exercise: Build meals around vegetables, fruit, whole grains, legumes, nuts and, if non-vegetarian, fish.
source: Source: American Heart Association; World Health Organization

text: Heart health diet and exercise: Limit saturated fat, trans fat, processed meat, added sugar and fried snacks.
source: Source: American Heart Association; World Health Organization

text: Heart health diet and exercise: Avoid trans fats such as partially hydrogenated oils and vanaspati.
source: Source: American Heart Association; World Health Organization

text: Heart health diet and exercise: Use small amounts of unsaturated oils instead of large amounts of ghee, butter or palm oil.
source: Source: American Heart Association; World Health Organization

text: Heart health diet and exercise: Keep salt below 5 grams (about one teaspoon) per day, including salt in pickles, papad and packaged foods.
source: Source: American Heart Association; World Health Organization

text: Heart health diet and exercise: Fatty fish about twice a week is recommended if you eat fish.
source: Source: American Heart Association; World Health Organization

text: Heart health diet and exercise: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate or 75 minutes of vigorous activity per week, plus muscle-strengthening on 2 days.
source: Source: American Heart Association; World Health Organization

text: Heart health diet and exercise: Stop smoking and tobacco use and limit alcohol.
source: Source: American Heart Association; World Health Organization

text: Heart health diet and exercise: Chest pain, severe breathlessness or fainting needs emergency care. Do not exercise through these symptoms.
source: Source: American Heart Association; World Health Organization

text: Heart health diet and exercise: People with known heart disease should speak to their doctor before starting a new exercise programme.
source: Source: American Heart Association; World Health Organization
